title: Bill Gillen, trumpeter at the Fern
summary: Hug and Allen discuss trumpeter Bill Gillen and how long he played.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you something about that trumpet player that was playing in front of you, Bill Gillan? Bill Gillan?

Bill Gillan was a very fine, very fine trumpet player. Played very, very good, uh, lead trumpet. Um, I think, uh, Bill, Bill, uh, would have been a really, a real fine, all-around, New Orleans man. Uh, of course, he gave it up. I don't know, he hasn't played for quite some time now. In fact, I don't think I've seen him probably ten years or so. Uh, Bill, Bill used to like Bix quite a lot in those days. Uh, in fact, he, uh, he imitated some of his solos quite well. And, uh, we used to kid him to the extent that we used to call him Bix sometimes, you know. He, he had, uh, a couple of solos that Bix did on jazz and blues down. He did, he did him quite well. But, uh, aside from imitating Bix, Bill was, uh, was a pretty good, uh, pretty good trumpet player in his own right.
When did he, uh, die? I mean, when did he stop playing?

Well, uh, far as I know of, he's still living. Mm-hm. But, uh, Bill, Bill's been out of the business, I imagine. I don't think Bill's played the past 25 years that I know of. He just, just quit playing all together, far as, far as I know. Unless...
Okay. That's a new name to me. Bill Gilliam, yeah. He was, he was pretty good, too.
Bill Bander when he took a... Yeah. ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...
Bill Gillen, you say he stopped about 25 years.

I would imagine so, Dick, unless he played around with small bands, maybe spot jogged around, that I never got in contact with him after that because I don't know if Bill ever belonged to the Musicians' Union. He may have, but I don't believe he did. So therefore, after I joined the union, actually, I got out of contact with him. But I don't believe that Bill played much after that.
Whose band was it at the Fern, anyway?
It was Von Gammon's band, the drummer.
And what other bands did Gillen play with that you know of?
